observations: Photo 0 shows a white industrial sewing machine on a long table with built-in controls; brand label on the machine head appears to read “Emel”.
Photo 0 shows a red/black tool box or accessory case on the table and a measuring tape hanging down the front.
Photo 1 shows the same machine from a different angle; the “Emel” label is visible on the head.
Photo 1 shows a small label on the machine body that looks like it may include a model/series code, but it is not clearly readable in the image provided.
No clear view of the exact machine type (e.g., overlock, buttonhole, industrial straight-stitch, etc.) beyond it being an industrial sewing machine.

claims.claim: 1 year used industrial machine working perfectly
claims.evidence: Photos show the machine installed and photographed, but there is no powered-on test, no running video, and no clear hour meter/maintenance record.

risks.risk: Machine may not be fully functional under load (timing, feed, motor drive, or stitch quality issues). Photos cannot confirm performance.
risks.proof: Short video of the machine running and sewing a straight line on fabric (showing feed movement and consistent stitches).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: needs service/repair).

risks.risk: Exact model/type is unclear; wrong machine type can change value significantly.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the model/serial plate (the small label on the machine body) and a photo of the machine head front to identify the machine type.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at a generic industrial sewing machine level (worst case: lower-spec/unknown type).

risks.risk: Missing/incorrect accessories or parts (presser feet, needles, bobbins, motor belt, wiring, foot pedal) can reduce usability.
risks.proof: Photo list of included accessories laid out (needles, bobbins, presser feet, foot pedal, power cable, any manuals) plus a photo showing the motor/belt connection.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming key accessories may be missing (worst case: buyer must source parts).

risks.risk: Electrical issues or control faults (power supply, speed control, pedal) not visible in photos.
risks.proof: Video showing power-on with speed control and foot pedal response (RPM changes) and no error lights.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as electrical/control not guaranteed (worst case: needs electrical check).

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up of the model/serial plate (the small label on the machine body) and confirm the exact machine type.
Send a short running video: power on + foot pedal + sewing on fabric (show stitch consistency).
Send photos of all included accessories (needles, bobbins, presser feet, foot pedal, power cable, any manuals).
Show the motor/belt connection and any control panel labels clearly.
response.reason: The photos confirm it is an Emel industrial sewing machine, but the seller’s “working perfectly” and the exact model/type are not provable from the images alone. To price safely for Lagos pickup, we need a powered-on sewing test and a readable model/serial plate.
